newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium, copper fall, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium, copper fall, slow trade.

text.p: Taipei base metal traders said on Tuesday that Taiwan's copper and aluminium products prices have fallen in recent days due to a slower seasonal demand.
Demand for aluminium ingots had dropped since late June as buyers covered their third-quarter demand through long-term supply contracts, traders said.
Taiwan's aluminium import premiums fell to US$90 per tonne over LME cash prices, down from $90-95 a week ago.
"The metal market is very quiet now," said a Japanese metal trader in Taipei. "We offered aluminium at $90 premium a tonne, but market is still slow."
Taiwan's third quarter long-term aluminium import premiums were settled in early June at US$90-95 per tonne over LME futures' prices, up from US$84-89 per tonne in the second quarter.

Taiwan copper import premiums were at $52-57 per tonne over LME cash prices, down from $55-60 per tonne a week ago as buying interest remained sluggish amid the recent copper futures rally, metal traders said.
"Demand for near-term copper supplies remain sluggish, so we have to lower our premium levels" a metal trader said.
Traders expected to see local copper market to resume a more active trading in September.
Near-term local copper wire and strip prices also declined in line with falling import premiums, traders said.
